prompt.context: The Dog Food Company manufactures dog food that sells in pet stores across the nation. The company has recently developed a new product that allows customers to test their dogs for genetic predisposition to various diseases and also reveals the dog's breeding history. The client's CEO needs our help to decide how to launch this new product into the US market.
prompt.question: What are the issues you would take into consideration to launch this product?

clarifying_info.a: It is a take-home kit of cotton swabs. Customers use the swabs to take a saliva sample, and then send the sample back to the company for analysis.

clarifying_info.q: What is the price of the product?
clarifying_info.a: The price is approximately $50. It is not a high-end product — it is quite affordable.

clarifying_info.q: Are there competitors or substitute products?
clarifying_info.a: The company has a patent for this product, valid for 10+ years, so there is no current threat of competitors.

clarifying_info.q: Should the market size answer be in dollars or units?
clarifying_info.a: Either is acceptable — clarify with the interviewer which they prefer.

framework: Market: characteristics, market size, willingness to pay
Target Customer: identify and segment potential buyers
Sales & Distribution: evaluate current distribution channels; assess need for new channels or additional/educated sales team
Finances: estimate reasonable volume and price (revenue); assess manufacturing setup costs and variable costs
Other: exit strategy, competitor response, future technological R&D

questions.prompt: Estimate the market size for this product in the US.
questions.guidance: Candidate should segment from US population down to purchasing dog owners, then multiply by price to get revenue. Should note whether the answer is in units (volume) or dollars (revenue). Strong candidates will also identify factors driving the purchase rate and note the one-time-use nature of the product.

math.setup: Segment US population into households, identify households with dogs, apply a purchase rate, then multiply by price.
steps: % of Households Owning Dogs: 20% → Dog-owning Households = 75,000,000 × 20% = 15,000,000
% of Dog Owners who Purchase Product: 50% → Products Purchased (volume) = 15,000,000 × 50% = 7,500,000

questions.guidance: Easy answers: mass consumer dog owners (family pets), dog breeders (dog races, show dogs), owners of trained dogs (police K-9, assistance dogs). Hard/bonus answers: doctors/vets (diagnose problems), animal shelters (make animals more desirable), pet stores (sell more animals).

questions.prompt: Prioritize your customer segments. Which would you target first? Why? How would you market to them?
questions.guidance: Target the mass consumer dog owner (families) first. Rationale: (1) The Dog Food Company already has marketing and distribution capabilities for dog food, making it more cost-efficient to treat this product similarly. (2) The mass consumer market is larger than other segments. (3) Mass consumers have less likelihood of already knowing the dog's breed compared to breeders or professional owners.

brainstorming.prompt: Who is your target customer for the genetic testing product?

categories.name: Professional/Commercial Dog Owners
ideas: Owners of trained dogs (police K-9, assistance dogs for the blind/disabled)

categories.name: Professional Services
ideas: Animal shelters — to make animals more desirable to adopters
Pet stores — to sell more animals by providing genetic information

recommendation: Our market size calculation shows a potential market of $375 million for the new genetic product.
The Dog Food Company should initially target the mass market of dog owners and leverage its existing distribution channel by placing the product in pet retail chains.
risks: Dogs will only need this genetic testing product once over a lifetime period, and many owners may purchase the product during the initial launch. Sales may boom in the first period, then decline and stabilize over time — long-run market shrinks to the replacement rate (new dogs each year).
Although the product has a patent, the company must stay abreast of competing products and substitute methods for obtaining genetic information.
next_steps: Develop a marketing campaign targeting the mass consumer.
Manufacture the product and get it into the distribution chain (leverage existing pet retail relationships).
